text:
Lina: Quick heads-up — saw eviction thrash on gpu-07 during a tenant microburst this morning. continuous-batcher kept shrinking slabs and then forcing KV evictions, which spiked P95 by ~3x :grimacing:
Sam: ugh. do we have a repro? metrics + a short trace would help.
Lina: putting logs here: `logs/redwood/gpu-07/2026-03-21/evict-thrash.txt`. Key pattern: 200ms bursts of small requests, then a big 1500-token request. batching window collapsed and slabs got aggressively rebalanced.
Jordan: are slabs allocated per-slot or global per-GPU?
Sam: currently per-GPU but with soft partitions per-tenant (heuristic). That heuristic lets fast tenants steal headroom when windows shrink.
Mike: sounds like two problems: (1) shrink-on-low-util triggers too fast, (2) eviction algo has low hysteresis. need a guard against rapid shrink/expand cycles.
Lina: agreed. Thinking of: elastic slabs that only shrink if underutilized for T_stable (30s) and apply a soft reservation for long-running KV owners.
Olivia: also KV warmup matters — when we evict and then get a big request we pay an O(1) latency tax for reload. Could we prefetch top-K keys on tenant window growth?
Jordan: prefetch is plausible but mustn't blow memory. Maybe prefetch up to 10% of slab capacity for that tenant, and background fill.
Sam: proposal sketch: 1) add shrink cooldown (T_cooldown = 30s), 2) hysteresis factor H = 1.25 for shrink (need 25% sustained slack to shrink), 3) reserve headroom R = 20% per GPU for sudden large requests.
Mike: +1. Also add an eviction score that penalizes recently-touch keys to avoid thrash. E.g. score = LRU_score * (1 + penalty_if_recent_resize).
Lina: wrote a tiny proto config to test, dropping here:
```
batcher.slab_elasticity = {
  cooldown_seconds: 30
  shrink_hysteresis: 1.25
  reserved_headroom_percent: 20
  eviction_penalty_window: 10s
}
```
Sam: looks good. how do we measure success? P95 latency, eviction rate, and cost (GPU memory pressure).
Olivia: add KV miss latency and number of cold fills per minute. Those directly capture warmup overhead.
Jordan: one wrinkle: multi-tenant GPU with tenants pinned to slots — reserved_headroom could reduce throughput for steady tenants. Might need tiered reservation: high-priority tenants get reserved slots, others compete for the remainder.
Mike: we can decouple: R_total = 20%, of that R_dynamic = 10% for burst absorb, R_reserved = 10% assigned by SLA tier.
Lina: action items: (1) Sam to implement cooldown + hysteresis flags behind a feature flag, (2) Jordan to add eviction-penalty hook, (3) Olivia to add KV warmup metrics. We'll run an A/B on a subset of nodes.
Sam: I'll attach feature flags under `batcher.elasticity` and add telemetry tags `experimental:slab_cooldown_v1`.
autoscale-bot: Experiment cluster provisioned: experiments/scheduler/slab-cooldown-v1 on 8 nodes (gpu-07..gpu-14).
Mike: we should also simulate the microburst pattern in the local loadgen: repeated small requests + occasional big request at ratio 20:1. If the simulation still thrashes we iterate.
Jordan: can we add a lightweight backpressure hint from router to batcher to avoid immediate shrink when router sees big pending requests?
Lina: yes — add a 'pending_long_request' flag in the enqueue metadata. Router can set it when it sees a queued large request. Batcher treats that as a temporary hold on shrink decisions.
Sam: note: need to ensure this flag isn't spoofable by arbitrary clients; router will only set it for internal routed requests.
Olivia: timeline? Sam, can you get a branch and deploy to experiment cluster today?
Sam: will do. target rollout to experiment cluster by EOD, run for 24h and collect P50/P95, eviction-rate, kv-cold-fills.
Lina: if experiment looks good we'll roll to a canary pool and run a week. If we see throughput loss >2% for steady tenants, rollback.
Mike: also capture cost impact: if reserved headroom reduces throughput we might need to tune R_reserved down.
Jordan: one more thought — metric to monitor: rapid resize count per minute. If >3 resizes/min we consider the node unstable and force a safe slab size.
Lina: nice. ok all — I'll pin this thread and add a short doc with the rationale + measurement plan: `docs/eng-runtime/slab-elasticity-experiment.md`.
Olivia: :thumbsup:
Sam: starting PR now -> will post link here when ready.
Lina: thanks all, good plan.
